title: A durable, broadly affordable total artificial heart

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a total artificial heart that replaces the pumping function of a failing heart and sustains ordinary life for many years. It would deliver adequate circulation as a person's needs change, balance blood flow through the lungs and the rest of the body, and combine dependable operation with acceptable rates of clotting, bleeding, infection and mechanical failure. The long-term objective is destination therapy for people with end-stage heart failure.

The concept includes the complete implanted and externally supported system. Anatomical fit, power supply, actuation, control, blood-contacting materials and maintenance must work together. Soft robotics and hybrid materials offer one research approach toward this objective. The broader innovation could be realized through any architecture that meets the clinical and practical requirements.

As a synthesis of the stated broad-access objective, affordability includes manufacturing, implantation, ongoing care, equipment servicing and lifetime financing. A technically successful pump would fulfill this concept only when patients in explicitly defined healthcare settings could obtain and sustain the complete treatment.

significance.text: A dependable artificial heart could provide long-term cardiac replacement without requiring a human donor heart. Because donor hearts are scarce, successful destination therapy could expand the available supply of replacement treatment and reduce dependence on donor availability. This consequence remains conditional on demonstrating durable clinical performance.

The potential benefit extends to the quality of life during support. Reliable circulation, fewer serious complications and practical power could allow patients to live with less disruption from their replacement system. The supplied paper identifies complications and quality-of-life limitations of available total artificial hearts and treats improved long-term support as a development goal. Its prototype results establish an experimental foundation for that goal.

As a conditional downstream synthesis, reproducible production and a sustainable clinical-service model could make cardiac replacement more widely available. The magnitude of that expansion would depend on patient eligibility, surgical capacity, follow-up services, lifetime costs and financing. Comparing the proposed device with donor transplantation would require defined patient populations and comparable outcomes. Blood-pumping performance alone cannot establish equivalent survival or quality of life.

missing_breakthrough.text: The unsolved capability is integrated, durable replacement under changing physiological demands. A device must maintain sufficient output and coordinate pulmonary and systemic circulation across ordinary activities and physiological changes. The supplied study reports adaptive behavior in laboratory testing, while dependable long-term operation of the complete system remains a development objective.

Blood compatibility and mechanical durability must be achieved together. The paper describes thromboembolic risks and bleeding associated with acquired von Willebrand disease or anticoagulation, alongside infection risks from percutaneous drivelines. Blood-contacting materials, flow behavior and moving structures must retain their performance over prolonged use. A pneumatic septum leak ended the reported acute goat experiment, providing a concrete example of a mechanical weakness requiring further development.

Power and anatomical integration remain substantial engineering barriers. The paper states that the complete fluidic circuit, electronics and transcutaneous energy-transfer system had yet to become fully implantable, and that device size and anatomical fit required further optimization. Its exploratory power-and-actuation integration operated in a mock circulation loop with low output. Translating that exploration into reliable support requires the integrated system to supply clinically adequate circulation while meeting implantation and power requirements.

As requirements derived from the concept, broadly affordable treatment also needs reproducible manufacturing, implantation, maintenance and follow-up. The supplied evidence leaves unresolved how these services would be organized and financed, what lifetime costs would be acceptable, and which healthcare settings could deliver the treatment at scale.

current_state.text: The supplied evidence centers on Maziar Arfaee, Annemijn Vis and colleagues' paper, A soft robotic total artificial hybrid heart, published in Nature Communications on 3 June 2025. Its introduction describes SynCardia and Carmat's Aeson as clinically available total artificial hearts and characterizes their implantation as sparse because of complications and quality-of-life limitations. The supplied text leaves the distribution of clinical indications, including the proportion used as a bridge to transplantation, unresolved.

In a dynamic laboratory test bench, the soft-robotic hybrid prototype achieved a maximum left ventricular output of 5.71 ± 0.04 liters per minute at 60 beats per minute, summarized in the abstract as approximately 5.7 liters per minute. The paper also reports adaptive behavior resembling an aspect of native cardiac function. These measurements describe in vitro performance and establish a bounded experimental achievement.

The animal experiments examined different levels of the technology. Rat studies tested coating materials as aortic vascular grafts. In an acute goat experiment, the pump supplied all circulation for 50 minutes, after which a leak in the pneumatic septum ended testing. Chronic integrated animal testing remained future work, and the study reports no long-term human replacement demonstration.

The study also explored a fully implantable control and powering concept through an initial mock-loop integration experiment. The reported low output and incomplete implantation of the full system limit what that experiment establishes. Taken together, the laboratory, component and acute-animal results support proof of concept, with substantial materials, durability and system-integration work remaining.

The supplied review assessed the retained full article text. Linked supplements, source data, movies and figure images were unavailable for that assessment, so the account here follows explicit textual results. The supplied freshness-search record was empty, leaving the field's status on 1 November 2026 unresolved. The source index records retrieval on 11 November 2026, which supplies an access date for the June 2025 paper. These access and coverage limits leave later developments open while preserving the dated experimental findings.

completion_criteria.text: A proposed convincing clinical demonstration would comprise multicenter studies with a prespecified duration of many years, defined patient populations and survival and quality-of-life outcomes comparable to donor transplantation in suitable populations. Complication thresholds should be specified in advance for thrombosis, bleeding, infection and mechanical failure, alongside clear accounting of device replacement and other interventions. These are proposed criteria for this concept, with follow-up duration and acceptable rates still requiring operational definitions.
completion_criteria.label: Multiyear multicenter survival and quality-of-life outcomes comparable to donor transplantation

completion_criteria.text: Proposed engineering demonstrations would establish adequate, adaptable circulation and balanced pulmonary and systemic support across a prespecified range of patient needs. They would also establish reliable power during ordinary activities and interruptions to external power, durable blood-contacting materials, mechanical reliability and anatomical fit within defined patient groups. Reproduction across devices and centers would strengthen the demonstration. Finite testing would establish performance within the tested conditions and populations.
completion_criteria.label: Adequate, adaptable and balanced circulation across prespecified patient needs

completion_criteria.text: A proposed broad-access demonstration would show reproducible manufacturing quality, implantation, servicing and follow-up in explicitly defined healthcare settings. Assessment would include total lifetime costs and the personnel, facilities and service capacity needed to sustain treatment. Any claim of broad affordability would require an explicit access benchmark and evidence that eligible patients can obtain continued care under the specified financing arrangements.
completion_criteria.label: Eligible patients obtain continued care against an explicit access benchmark

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis connects CAR-03 most closely with three other routes to restoring a usable heart. CAR-01, Regenerate a severely damaged adult human heart, aims to recover the patient's own living heart. CAR-04, A dependable supply of transplantable animal hearts, seeks replacement through animal organs. CAR-07, Produce a transplantable, fully engineered living human heart, seeks a manufactured living organ. CAR-03 pursues artificial pumping replacement, bringing its own requirements for power, blood compatibility and mechanical durability. These concepts share a potential role in severe cardiac failure while retaining distinct biological and engineering objectives.

Roster-based synthesis places CAR-05, Correct inherited heart disease directly and durably in the beating heart, and CAR-08, Durably reverse heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, alongside CAR-03 through their potential to improve cardiac function. CAR-05 targets inherited disease within the heart, and CAR-08 targets a specific heart-failure syndrome. CAR-03 addresses replacement when artificial support is suitable. Its clinical eligibility and comparative benefit for those disease groups would require separate evidence.

Roster-based synthesis links CAR-02, Reliably reverse advanced atherosclerosis throughout the arterial tree, CAR-10, Reverse established calcific aortic stenosis without valve replacement, and CAR-11, Reverse pulmonary arterial hypertension and its cardiovascular consequences, through the circulation that an artificial heart must support. These concepts target arterial disease, aortic-valve disease and pulmonary vascular disease respectively. Their relationship to CAR-03 concerns the condition of the wider cardiovascular system and the demands placed on replacement pumping.

Roster-based synthesis connects CAR-06, Make most preventable sudden cardiac deaths predictable and preventable, and CAR-09, A durable, non-ablative cure for atrial fibrillation, through cardiac risk and rhythm disorders. CAR-06 concerns prediction and prevention of fatal events, and CAR-09 concerns a durable rhythm cure. CAR-03 concerns sustained artificial circulation. Its completion criteria would establish replacement-system performance, while claims about broader prevention or rhythm treatment would need their own demonstrations.

Roster-based synthesis connects CAR-12, Detect actionable coronary plaque risk before a first clinical event, and CAR-13, Broadly prevent cardiac injury from cancer treatment without weakening cancer control, through the possibility of preventing damage that could contribute to later cardiac failure. CAR-12 focuses on earlier risk detection and CAR-13 on treatment-associated injury prevention. CAR-03 provides a potential replacement pathway for suitable patients with established severe failure. The supplied evidence leaves the effect of either preventive innovation on future artificial-heart demand unquantified.

unresolved_issues: The supplied record cannot establish the field's status on 1 November 2026 or identify developments after the June 2025 paper.
The predominant clinical indications for available total artificial hearts remain unresolved in the supplied evidence.
Linked supplements, source data, movies and figure images were outside the supplied review's inspection scope.
Long-term integrated durability, chronic animal performance and multi-year human outcomes for the reported hybrid prototype remain unestablished in this record.
Prespecified support duration, eligible populations, transplant-comparison methods and acceptable complication rates remain to be defined for the proposed completion criteria.
Lifetime costs, affordability benchmarks, financing arrangements and healthcare settings capable of broad delivery remain unvalidated.

brief.title: An affordable replacement heart that lasts for years
possible: People whose hearts can no longer pump enough blood could live for years with an artificial replacement. They could go about ordinary activities while it adjusts blood flow to their changing needs.
Patients could obtain and sustain the whole treatment, including surgery, power equipment, servicing and ongoing care, at an affordable lifetime cost.
why: Donor hearts are scarce. A dependable artificial heart could give more people with severe heart failure access to long-term replacement treatment.
Reliable pumping, fewer serious complications and practical power supplies could make daily life less disrupted by treatment.

sources.who: Maziar Arfaee, Annemijn Vis and colleagues
sources.showed: Their soft robotic heart pumped blood and adjusted its output in laboratory tests. It also briefly supplied all circulation in a goat before a leak ended testing.
sources.quote: In vitro, the Hybrid Heart pumps 5.7 L/min and mimics the native heart’s adaptive function.
sources.cited_for: This supports the feasibility of a soft artificial heart that adapts its pumping in laboratory conditions.
sources.not_established: The complete system still needs long-term animal testing and durable human support.

sources.who: Robert D. Dowling, Laman A. Gray and colleagues
sources.showed: A small trial of the fully implanted AbioCor heart achieved balanced circulation and allowed some patients to leave hospital. Deaths and serious complications occurred.
sources.quote: There have been no significant device malfunctions.
sources.cited_for: This supports the feasibility of fully implanted replacement and life outside hospital.
sources.not_established: The small trial did not establish lasting survival and quality of life comparable to donor transplantation.

sources.showed: Researchers reviewed SynCardia patients who had already survived beyond a year on support. Most reached donor transplantation, while infections, bleeding and device failures occurred.
sources.quote:
Five patients (10%) had a 
device failure reported.
sources.cited_for: This documents prolonged artificial-heart support and its complications.
sources.not_established: Selecting patients who already survived prolonged support leaves overall long-term survival and permanent replacement unresolved.

sources.who: Jack G. Copeland and the CardioWest Total Artificial Heart Investigators
sources.showed: More artificial-heart recipients survived to donor transplantation than patients in a comparison group. The study used historical controls and did not randomly assign treatment.
sources.quote: Eighty-one patients received the artificial-heart device.
sources.cited_for: This supports artificial hearts as a way to keep critically ill patients alive until transplantation.
sources.not_established: Survival until donor transplantation does not establish durable replacement for patients who will keep the device.

sources.showed: A single patient received the Aeson heart, which automatically adjusts pumping. He went home and later received a donor heart.
sources.quote: The patient was successfully bridged to transplant after 5 months of support on the device and has made a full recovery.
sources.cited_for: This demonstrates human support with automatically adjusted pumping and discharge home.
sources.not_established: A single case cannot establish lasting safety, and reported manufacturing defects raise questions about consistent production.

shown: Artificial hearts have kept people alive until donor transplantation and allowed some to return home. Torregrossa and colleagues documented support beyond a year, although their study included only patients who had already survived that long.

Arfaee, Vis and colleagues tested a soft robotic approach. It supplied a goat’s entire circulation for 50 minutes before a leak ended the experiment. Long-term testing of the complete system remains ahead.
missing: The complete system still needs to sustain ordinary life for many years with acceptable complication rates.
Reliable power, anatomical fit and balanced blood flow through the lungs and body still need to work together across changing demands.
Blood-contacting surfaces and moving parts still need to retain their performance over prolonged use.
Consistent manufacturing and affordable lifelong care still need demonstration in defined healthcare settings.

milestones.label: Long-term survival and quality of life match donor transplantation
milestones.explanation: Studies across hospitals would have to show comparable survival and quality of life over many years, with agreed complication limits. This would establish lasting clinical benefit.

milestones.label: The complete heart system meets changing bodily needs
milestones.explanation: Testing would have to show adaptable, balanced circulation, reliable power, durable materials and mechanical parts, and anatomical fit across defined patient needs. This would establish dependable everyday support.

milestones.label: Eligible patients can afford and sustain treatment
milestones.explanation: Defined healthcare settings would have to deliver consistent manufacturing, surgery, servicing and lifelong care against an explicit access benchmark. This would establish that eligible patients can obtain continued treatment.

uncertain: The required follow-up duration, eligible patient groups and acceptable complication rates remain to be defined.
Fair comparisons with donor transplantation need agreed patient groups and outcome measures.
Acceptable lifetime costs, financing arrangements and benchmarks for broad access remain unresolved.

page.title: Total artificial heart destination therapy
page.definition: A mechanical circulatory support system replaces both ventricles, the heart chambers that pump blood to the lungs and body, as permanent treatment for irreversible failure of both sides. The complete system has demonstrated safety and effectiveness for this destination-therapy indication.

goal.need: NHLBI reports that 60–80% of total artificial heart recipients survive to donor transplantation, while fewer than 60% of recipients who are not transplanted survive one year after surgery. Permanent replacement addresses patients with failure of both ventricles who cannot receive a donor heart.

figures.caption: Total artificial heart outcomes summarized by NHLBI on 12 April 2023
rows: Survival for one year after surgery
Recipients who do not receive a transplant
figures.note: These are different outcomes and populations. The page does not supply cohort sizes or observation years.

statements.body: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute
statements.quote: Researchers are working on total artificial heart devices that may be used as treatments for people who cannot have a transplant.
ultimately obtain indication for use as destination therapy (DT) and obtain PMA in the United States.
statements.context: The company's 2022 Universal Registration Document describes its clinical development objectives. PMA means FDA premarket approval.

completion.title: The FDA grants a total artificial heart premarket approval for destination therapy.
completion.criterion: The FDA grants premarket approval for a complete total artificial heart system explicitly intended for permanent cardiac replacement, including use in patients ineligible for transplantation. Approval requires valid scientific evidence establishing safety and effectiveness for that intended use. A bridge-to-transplant approval or humanitarian device exemption does not satisfy this test. The general PMA standard specifies no universal survival percentage, follow-up duration or treatment-cost ceiling.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Premarket Approval framework; CARMAT explicitly identifies destination therapy and US PMA as development objectives.
completion.threshold_quote: sufficient valid scientific evidence to assure that the device is safe and effective for its intended use(s).
completion.basis: This tests authorization for permanent replacement under the FDA's safety-and-effectiveness standard. Humanitarian exemptions waive effectiveness requirements. AbioCor received such an exemption on 5 September 2006; SynCardia's approval on 15 October 2004 covered bridging to transplantation. Neither establishes this completion test. PMA alone would not establish affordability or a specified multi-year service life.

milestones.title: A total artificial heart achieves 80% six-month bench reliability at 60% confidence.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate at least 80% system reliability over six months at 60% confidence under representative physiological conditions. The Japanese guidance recommends considering 80% confidence and continuing testing for at least two years. Volume-displacement: FDA reported 88% one-year reliability at 90% confidence for 11 SynCardia units, totaling 6,715 device-days. Rotary: a BiVACOR study published on 17 September 2025 tested blood loops for six hours at 5 L/min and 100 mmHg, with six tests per flow mode; it does not establish six-month reliability.
milestones.set_by: METI/AIST artificial-heart development working group, Development Guidelines 2007, section 12; a Japanese development benchmark covering ventricular assist devices and total artificial hearts.
milestones.threshold_quote: 最低限 80% reliability, 60% confidence level で 6 ヶ月

milestones.title: Total artificial hearts support five calves for 30 days without embolic or wireless-power injury.
milestones.criterion: At least five calves weighing 90–120 kg complete 30 days under Good Laboratory Practice, with elective termination, freedom from thromboembolic complications and no tissue injury from transcutaneous energy transmission. FDA recorded 14 AbioCor calves completing 30 days. The Hybrid Heart paper published on 3 June 2025 reports one goat supported for 50 minutes before a pneumatic leak. Its laboratory output was 5.71 ± 0.04 L/min at 60 beats/min, from three experiments using one prototype. Neither Hybrid Heart result meets this chronic-animal test.
milestones.set_by: FDA, H040006 section 9.2; the published preclinical protocol was specific to the volume-displacement AbioCor system.
milestones.threshold_quote: a minimum of five calf implants for the duration of 30-days

milestones.title: Two five-patient cohorts each have a 60-day artificial-heart survivor without significant complications.
milestones.criterion: At least one recipient in each of the first two five-patient cohorts survives 60 days without significant complications before enrollment continues. FDA's AbioCor review recorded 10 of 14 recipients surviving beyond 60 days; survival alone does not establish the complication condition. The initial seven-patient AbioCor publication reported two hospital discharges. For rotary pumps, one BiVACOR recipient received support from 9 July 2024 until donor transplantation on 17 July 2024, according to a 26 July 2024 press release; that result was not peer reviewed.
milestones.set_by: FDA, H040006 section 10; the enrollment-continuation criterion was specific to AbioCor's first human study.
milestones.threshold_quote: one patient in each group surviving to 60 days without significant complications.

milestones.title: Total artificial heart recipients are alive and ambulatory 30 days after donor transplantation.
milestones.criterion: Treatment success requires survival to 30 days after donor transplantation, New York Heart Association functional class I or II, ambulation, no ventilator dependence and no dialysis. In the SynCardia pivotal cohort, 56 of 81 recipients met this composite endpoint. The peer-reviewed study reported survival to transplantation of 79% versus 46% among 35 historical controls. These are bridge-to-transplant results; survival after transplantation includes support from the donor heart.
milestones.set_by: FDA, P030011 clinical protocol and effectiveness review; the composite endpoint was specific to the volume-displacement SynCardia bridge-to-transplant study.
milestones.threshold_quote: Treatment success was defined as patients who, at 30 days post transplant, were

milestones.title: A total artificial heart meets a six-month destination-therapy endpoint in at least 8 of 19 patients.
milestones.criterion: In the registered primary arm, at least eight of 19 patients must be alive at six months on the original artificial heart without permanent disabling stroke deficits, or have become transplant eligible or undergone transplantation. Absence of disabling stroke is defined by a modified Rankin Scale score of 0–2. The protocol also evaluates adverse events against device-specific performance goals. This is an HDE-supporting endpoint, and its transplant-related alternatives do not demonstrate permanent artificial-heart support.
milestones.set_by: SynCardia Systems, registered protocol NCT02232659; specific to the 70 cc volume-displacement SynCardia device. Sponsor-submitted registry text is reproduced by Veeva.
milestones.threshold_quote: eight of the 19 subjects either must be alive at six months on the original TAH-t implant

milestones.title: Clinical studies establish a total artificial heart’s benefit–risk balance for destination therapy.
milestones.criterion: Clinical evidence establishes clinically significant results in a significant portion of the intended destination-therapy population, with probable benefits outweighing probable risks. FDA principally requires well-controlled investigations; its general standard specifies no numerical survival endpoint. A 2014 SynCardia retrospective series selected 47 patients at ten centers who had already reached one year of support: median support was 554 days, range 365–1,373 days, with five device failures. This survivor-selected series cannot establish outcomes from implantation in a destination-therapy population.
milestones.set_by: FDA, PMA Clinical Studies, Safety and Effectiveness sections, applying 21 CFR 860.7; the general clinical-evidence standard preceding a PMA decision.

not_found: No external lifetime-cost or patient-access threshold for broadly affordable total artificial heart treatment was found in regulator, agency, standards or developer searches.
No universal numerical multi-year survival or quality-of-life completion threshold was found in regulator, programme, standards or developer searches.
No published outcome report for NCT02232659 or pivotal rotary total artificial heart destination-therapy cohort was found.
ClinicalTrials.gov opened without the NCT02232659 study text; the sponsor-submitted text was available in Veeva's reproduction.
Rotary total artificial heart animal-study conference reports were located at JHLT and ASAIO, but their full texts could not be opened.
The supplied SynCardia beyond-one-year PDF could not be opened; its abstract was available through an author's institutional publication record.

results.finding: One Hybrid Heart prototype ran for more than two hours in a bench experiment.
results.detail: The experiment used physiological pressures to check durability for an acute animal test; it did not establish six-month reliability or a confidence level.
results.quote: Prior to the animal trial, we conducted an in vitro experiment against physiological pressures using the exact same prototype for more than two hours (>7000 cycles), to ensure its durability within the time range of an acute animal experiment.

results.finding: One reported goat received Hybrid Heart support for 50 minutes.
results.detail: The acute experiment ended after a pneumatic septum leak. It did not test five calves for 30 days or establish the required freedom from complications and wireless-power injury.
results.quote: After de-airing and weaning from cardiopulmonary bypass, the Hybrid Heart was fully responsible for all blood flow in the goat during a 50 min testing period.

results.finding: In the seven-patient AbioCor series, two patients died after 60 days of support.
results.detail: The report does not establish a complication-free 60-day survivor in each of the first two five-patient cohorts. It describes multiple serious morbidities.
results.quote: There were 3 late deaths: one caused by multiple systems organ failure (postoperative day 56), one caused by a cerebrovascular accident (postoperative day 142), and one caused by retroperitoneal bleeding and resultant multiple systems organ failure (postoperative day 151).

results.finding: In the seven-patient AbioCor destination-therapy series, two patients were discharged from hospital.
results.detail: The early series reports serious morbidities and deaths; it does not establish the benefit–risk balance for the intended population.
results.quote: Three patients have taken multiple (>50) trips out of the hospital, and 2 have been discharged from the hospital.

results.finding: Of 34 transplanted SynCardia recipients, 3 died at a median of 145 days after transplantation.
results.detail: The reported range of 50–328 days indicates that these three survived at least 30 days after transplantation. The study does not establish the full 30-day functional and clinical composite endpoint.
results.quote:
Of the 34 patients who underwent cardiac transplantation, 
three patients died at a median time of 145 days (range 50–328 
days); graft rejection was the cause of death in all of them.

results.finding: Among 47 long-term SynCardia recipients, median artificial-heart support was 554 days.
results.detail: The retrospective series selected patients who had already survived more than one year on support. It cannot establish outcomes from implantation or the benefit–risk balance in the intended destination-therapy population.
results.quote:
The median support time was 554 days (1.5 years) (range 
365–1,374 days) and cumulative support time was 79.8 years.

results.finding: CardioWest recipients: 69% of 81 patients achieved treatment success.
results.detail: Treatment success required survival, NYHA class I or II, ambulation, no ventilator dependence and no dialysis 30 days after transplantation.
results.quote:
Treatment success was
achieved in 69 percent of the patients who received
an implant, as compared with 37 percent of the
controls (P=0.002).

results.finding: One Aeson recipient survived to transplantation after 5 months of support.
results.detail: This single case does not establish the required outcomes in two five-patient cohorts or freedom from significant complications through day 60. The paper's comment section inconsistently states eight months of support.
results.quote: After 5 months on support, a donor organ became available, and he underwent uncomplicated redo sternotomy, removal of the TAH, and cardiac transplantation.

results.finding: One Aeson recipient was alive 8 months after transplantation.
results.detail: The report does not establish the full 30-day composite, including functional class, ambulation, and freedom from ventilator dependence and dialysis.
results.quote: At 8 months after transplantation, there are no signs of allograft dysfunction or significant rejection.

results.finding: One Aeson recipient underwent transplantation after 5 months of artificial-heart support.
results.detail: The recipient was already transplant eligible, and this was a bridge-to-transplant early feasibility case, not a result from the specified 19-patient destination-therapy primary arm.
results.quote: After 5 months on support, a donor organ became available, and he underwent uncomplicated redo sternotomy, removal of the TAH, and cardiac transplantation.

results.finding: Penn State/3M electric total artificial heart, sample size not stated: 96.1% one-year reliability.
results.detail: Reliability was calculated using reliability growth principles after mock-loop testing and redesigns. The text does not describe the loop conditions sufficiently to establish that they were physiologically representative, or identify the pump as volume-displacement.
results.quote: The 1 and 2 year reliability of the Penn State/3M ETAH was shown to be 96.1% and 59.9%, respectively, at 80% confidence.

results.finding: SynCardia CardioWest TAH-t: 11 units achieved 88% one-year reliability at 90% confidence.
results.detail: The in-vitro tests accumulated 6,715 device-days without device-related failures. The source does not specify the physiological conditions used for the reliability tests.

The GLP protocol specified calves weighing 90–120 kg. All terminations were elective; implant courses were uncomplicated, with no evidence of thromboembolic problems. FDA anticipated no TET thermal injury problems.
results.quote:
Fourteen calves completed the 30-day implant study duration. Terminations were
elective. The implant courses of these studies were uncomplicated.

results.finding: BiVACOR rotary total artificial heart: five calves were supported for 30 days before elective termination.
results.detail: Calves weighed 82–108 kg, so the reported range extends below the criterion. The abstract does not establish GLP conditions or absence of transcutaneous energy transmission injury; it reports no significant device-related thrombi, not freedom from all thromboembolic complications.
results.quote: The BiVACOR TAH was implanted into five calves (82 - 108 kg) for 30 days before elective termination.

results.finding: One Australian BiVACOR recipient received artificial-heart support for 105 days.
results.detail: The patient received a transplant after 105 days. The release does not establish survival without significant complications or a qualifying survivor in each of the first two five-patient cohorts.
results.quote:
